A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniZyme and retain the same central framework. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including their appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not constitute missing material.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix D report original supervised and zero-shot experiments, ablations, hyperparameter analyses, HIV predictions and active-site prediction results.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report expanded cleavage-site experiments and original active-site comparisons, transfer, robustness, attribution, runtime and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The biochemical transformer, active-site pretraining, active-site-aware pooling, substrate encoder and joint prediction losses remain. Appendix C newly specifies the pooling function's Gaussian expansion and MLP implementation, but does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from three supervised and two zero-shot enzyme families to 69 and 23, respectively. Appendix G adds EC-number classification as a transfer task. Active-site prediction already appeared in v1; the underlying MEROPS and UniProt training sources remain.

E2.justification: DeepCleave and DeepDigest become evaluated supervised baselines, while Procleave disappears from the reported comparisons despite remaining cited. Appendix D adds GraphEC and NodeCoder as active-site prediction comparators. CAT3, ScreenCap3, ProsperousPlus and the adapted ReactZyme/ClipZyme comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported supervised split changes from 80/20 to 70/10/20. Zero-shot separation tightens from an 80% sequence-similarity threshold to below 60%, explicitly excluding training and pretraining enzymes. v3 also introduces aggregate ranking metrics and an active-site comparison reporting precision, recall and F1. These protocol revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and lambda sensitivity analysis, v3 adds structural-source stratification, confidence-bin and gradient-attribution analyses, active-site versus random perturbations, computational comparisons and an entropy-based failure analysis. Appendix J additionally reports component ablations aggregated across the expanded enzyme coverage.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different random seeds. v3 adds four two-sample t-tests across enzyme families, reporting t-statistics and p-values in Appendix F/Table 11. It does not document increased repetitions, and its main table captions no longer explicitly define the retained ± notation as standard deviation.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive family-level results, including average PR-AUC of 79.3% supervised and 71.1% zero-shot, plus new transfer and supplementary-analysis outcomes. Some earlier entries remain, including C14.003's tabulated 45.9% PR-AUC. Earlier cleavage ROC/PR curves and detailed ablation entries are removed. Revised protocols and conflicting presentations preclude interpreting the expansion as direct performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly formalizes the previously unspecified pooling function through a Gaussian probability embedding and MLP, in Equations 13–14. The prediction problem, frustration definitions, attention equations and objectives otherwise remain equivalent; neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified cleavage-site predictor, biochemical and active-site enhancement, and generalization to seen and unseen enzymes. The expanded experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the headline contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds substantive mechanistic and causal interpretations of attribution and perturbation results. Appendix K introduces an entropy/metal-coordination explanation for M10.003 failures and corresponding future improvements. The HIV figure now explicitly identifies P00698 as lacking ground truth, qualifying the earlier presentation of successful predictions.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the pooling implementation, adds dataset-license information and reports training/inference times. Reported hardware changes from eight A100 GPUs to eight 48-GB A6000 GPUs. The code pointer changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Most existing optimizer, embedding, preprocessing and stopping details remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds Protap benchmarking context and newer geometric-model references; the appendices introduce active-site predictor and protease-mechanism literature. Some earlier background and HIV references disappear. The central positioning against enzyme-specific cleavage predictors remains.

P1.justification: v3 tightens introductory prose, combines hydrolysis and active-site preliminaries, folds the HIV case study into zero-shot evaluation and rewrites parts of related work. Supplementary topics receive dedicated sections, while much of the method exposition and conclusion remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and comparison tables are substantially restructured around PR-AUC and family aggregates. New family-level plots and supplementary tables replace the earlier cleavage ROC/PR panels. The architecture, original ablation, sensitivity and active-site plots are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader coverage, stricter reported holdouts, additional comparators and supporting analyses address important weaknesses of v1. However, v3 introduces unresolved reporting and interpretation problems: Table 4 gives C14.003 supervised PR-AUC as 45.9%, while Figure 3 plots approximately 60%, and Appendix H extends model-attribution and pooling-perturbation evidence into claims of biological mechanistic causality. These conflicts affect central evidence, preventing a confident judgment that the substantial additions yield a net quality improvement.
